text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 2234-CTX: sudden spike in inference errors for dedicated clusters in eu-west-1. Error signature: KV_CACHE_MISMATCH / seq-offset drift. 90s rolling error rate = 6.8% (baseline 0.04%). Triggered on continuous-batching path.

alice: I'm on it — taking pager. Can someone post a quick provenance of recent runtime deploys?

ben: I pushed a micro-optimization to the KV reuse layer ~3h ago (PR #8241) that changed how seq offsets are loaded for paged KV entries. Rolling back diff now if we confirm.

carla: Observed customer reports from AcmeRetail and FinchAnalytics — outputs truncated or repeating tokens mid-response, looks like wrong KV values being reused across requests. Affected traffic mostly on dedicated pools with high concurrency.

alice: Repro steps (from logs):
```
request id=rb-9a2
model=synth-13b-v2
cache_lookup: page=42 seq_offset=1203 -> value:vX
response tokens: ... <drop> ... then duplicates of previous response
```
Seems seq_offset being read as previous session's offset occasionally.

ben: That matches a race in the paged-handoff path I introduced — a stale pointer could be returned if a page moved between batch windows. I'm preparing a hotfix to force copy-on-read for the reuse fast-path.

derek: Customer impact: AcmeRetail reported a live checkout assistant producing wrong product descriptions for ~150 sessions. We're escalating — CSMs already notified. Need ETA for mitigation.

alice: Mitigation options:
- A: disable KV reuse fast-path across all dedicated pools (quick config flip) — will increase latency but stops incorrect reuse.
- B: patch runtime to validate seq-offsets on lookup (safer but needs build & deploy).
- C: tighten continuous-batcher concurrency limit per GPU to reduce races (config change).

carla: Ops suggestion: flip to A for eu-west-1 only, and throttle continuous-batcher concurrently in other regions. Minimizes blast radius.

ben: I'll prepare the hotfix for B in parallel but recommend A as immediate stopgap. I can push the rollback of PR #8241 to eu-west-1 in ~8m.

ops-bot: Submitted infra change: `redwood-config/dedicated/eu-west-1 -> kv_reuse.enabled: false` (change id infra-cc-991). Waiting for approval.

alice: Approving infra change now. Do it. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: infra change applied to 6/6 nodes in eu-west-1. Rolling restart of serving pods started.

ben: Rolling restart completed in eu-west-1. Observability: error rate dropped to 0.12% within 45s of first pod restart.

carla: Confirmed with customer telemetry: AcmeRetail error submissions dropped to 0 after the restart window. FinchAnalytics still reports sporadic issues in us-central-1.

alice: Who's taking us-central-1? I can stay on eu-west-1 monitoring for 20m then handoff.

ben: I'll take us-central-1. For safety I'm going to also bump `continuousBatcher.max_in_flight` from 64 -> 32 on dedicated pools in non-prod first, then prod if stable. That avoids the page-handoff pressure.

derek: Noting external comms: CSMs will draft a short status to AcmeRetail explaining root cause = cached seq-offset reuse bug, immediate mitigation applied (kv_reuse disabled), and next steps (patch + rollout). Keep me posted on ETA for patch.

ben: ETA for proper fix (patch + canary + global rollout) ~4–6 hours. I'll open a release candidate now and run unit + integration tests.

carla: Temporary mitigation checklist:
- [x] Disable kv_reuse in eu-west-1
- [x] Roll restarts completed
- [x] CSM notified
- [ ] Throttle continuous batcher in us-central-1 (ben)
- [ ] Final patch and canary rollout (ben)

alice: Handoff: I'm handing pager to ben at T+30m. I'll stay available for callbacks for another hour. Ben, confirm you accept?

ben: I accept. Will update channel when us-central-1 throttle done.

ops-bot: Change applied: `redwood-config/dedicated/us-central-1 -> continuousBatcher.max_in_flight: 32` (change id infra-cc-992).

ben: Throttle applied to us-central-1. Early signals: error rate dipping from 3.1% -> 0.9% in 70s. Latency p95 increased by +12ms (acceptable tradeoff).

carla: Running post-mortem checklist and starting incident doc. Key notes so far for the doc: regression introduced by PR #8241, root cause = reuse fast-path didn't validate seq offsets after page handoffs, immediate mitigation was disabling reuse and throttling batcher, full fix requires copy-on-read + seq validation.

derek: Also flag commercial impact: two paying customers affected (AcmeRetail, FinchAnalytics) — estimate ~200 sessions with degraded outputs, no data exfiltration. We'll prepare a customer-facing summary.

alice: Thanks team. Ben, please open the release PR number and link here when ready. Also capture monitoring alerts to avoid noisy pages once we re-enable reuse.

ben: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/8247 (hotfix: seq-validate-on-lookup). I'll canary in staging then eu-west-1 with reuse enabled but seq validation on.

incident-bot: Incident 2234-CTX status -> mitigated (eu-west-1 hotfix applied, us-central throttled). Severity: S2. Follow-up task created: INC-2234-postmortem.

carla: Assigning postmortem to ben + alice. Draft due EOD.

ben: A couple notes to include in postmortem: add unit tests for paged-handoff race, add e2e that simulates high-concurrency reuse, and add a small metric that exposes seq-offset validation failures.

alice: Handing off pager to ben now. Leaving channel but monitoring for 15m.

ben: Acknowledged. I'll close the incident channel when postmortem is linked and customers notified.

carla: Thanks — closing active operations. We'll keep a follow-up thread for the postmortem edits. (added :white_check_mark:)
